items.title: Herb Ellis interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: The person who plays that best is George Van Eps. He made that style popular. He’s a great guitarist.

ctx.x: Well the two main stylists I believe would be Charlie Christian and Django Reinhardt. And Charlie is more right in the face, you know bang, just lay it right in there. And Django sort of flirts with it. I don’t mean that negatively. He plays a lot more notes than Charlie would play. And Charlie doesn’t need to play that many because he can say it with just a few you see. So that’s the two definite schools. And people can play a little bit

of both schools, but it usually comes from, you lean towards one school or another one. And then there are chordal players that play, when they have a solo they play chords. And maybe a couple of notes alone and then the chords. They are chord stylists. And there are not too many of those. The person who plays that best is George Van Eps. He made that style popular. He’s a great guitarist. Still playing. He’s even older than I am and that’s hard to do.
Tell us a little about that story you told us you were going to tell us about the Dorsey band.
